extract: Ashenvale, also known as Ashenvale Forest, is a wilderness region south of Darkshore and Felwood, west of Azshara, and north of the Stonetalon Mountains and the Barrens. It is the ancestral homeland of the night elves, under the protection of their Sentinels and the children of the demigod Cenarius,  with Astranaar as their main settlement. Since the Third War, the Horde has expanded their influence in the eastern part of the woods, with Splintertree Post as their main base of operations. The region is heavily populated with furbolgs, satyr, and wild creatures such as spiders, wolves, and bears.

{{Combat}} [[Dor'Danil Barrow Den]] | affiliation = [[Darnassus (nation)|Nation of Darnassus]], [[Alliance]], [[Durotar (nation)|Nation of Durotar]], [[Horde]], [[Furbolg|Furbolg tribes]] | faffiliation = [[Burning Legion]], [[Emerald Nightmare]], [[Nazjatar Empire]] | loc = Southwestern [[Northern Kalimdor]] | territory = Contested }} '''Ashenvale''', also known as '''Ashenvale Forest''',[[Hero's Call: Stonetalon Mountains!]][[Warcraft III]] maps is a wilderness region south of [[Darkshore]] and [[Felwood]], west of [[Azshara]], and north of the [[Stonetalon Mountains]] and the [[Barrens]]. It is the ancestral homeland of the [[Night elf|night elves]], under the protection of their [[Sentinels]] and the [[Cenarius#Children|children]] of the [[demigod]] [[Cenarius]], with [[Astranaar]] as their main settlement. Since the [[Third War]], the [[Horde]] has expanded their influence in the eastern part of the woods, with [[Splintertree Post]] as their main base of operations. The region is heavily populated with [[furbolg]]s, [[satyr]], and wild creatures such as [[spider]]s, [[Wolf|wolves]], and [[bear]]s. ==History== ===After the Sundering=== Not much is known about Ashenvale prior to the [[War of the Ancients]], but it was said that [[Xavius]] had a tower within the forest.[[Lady Benel'derath#Quotes|Lady Benel'derath's gossip]] After the [[Great Sundering]] in 10,000 [[BDP]], the burgeoning night elf society expanded into the dense forests of Ashenvale, slowly rebuilding their society over a few centuries.{{Ref WoWCV1|114}} During the [[War of the Satyr]] in 9,300 BDP, Ashenvale was ablaze by the [[satyr]]s' destructive [[fel]] magics as they struck with but one goal; the utter destruction of kaldorei civilization. After the [[Lords of the Emerald Flame]] were defeated, the [[Cenarion Circle]] fought against the [[Druids of the Scythe]], leading to the death of [[Mel'Thandris Starsong]], who sacrificed herself to save her fellow night elves from the [[worgen]]. After the battle, she and the [[Scythe of Elune]] were subsequently buried at the [[Shrine of Mel'Thandris]] in Ashenvale.''[[Curse of the Worgen Issue 2]]'' Around 7,300 [[BDP]], the [[Highborne]] declared the [[druid]]s cowards for refusing to wield the [[arcane]], and while [[Malfurion Stormrage|Archdruid Malfurion]] warned them that any use of magic would be punished, [[Dath'Remar Sunstrider]]'s followers unleashed a terrible magical storm upon Ashenvale in an attempt to protest against these restrictions. As the kaldorei could not bring themselves to put so many of their kin to death, they instead decided to exile them from their lands, cutting them off from the [[Well of Eternity (Hyjal)|Well of Eternity]]'s energies.{{Ref WoWCV1|117|118}} When the [[Long Vigil]] began, Archdruid Malfurion and his druids entered the [[Emerald Dream]], while [[Tyrande Whisperwind|High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind]] and her [[Sentinel]]s continued to patrol Ashenvale. For centuries, the [[Keeper of the grove|keepers of the grove]] kept close watch on the night elves and regularly helped the Sentinels maintain peace across the land, while the [[dryad]]s often appeared in the open with increasing frequency.[[The Sentinels and the Long Vigil]] Their presence in the wilds of Ashenvale was seen as an omen of better times to come.{{Ref WoWCV1|119}} Around 4,500 BDP, the Cenarion Circle discovered the existence of [[saronite]], and a group led by [[Fandral Staghelm]] decided to eradicate it. They secretly cut six enchanted branches from the boughs of [[Nordrassil]], then traveled the world to locations where saronite blooms had sprung to life, where they planted the branches to thwart the corruption. These areas included Ashenvale, [[Crystalsong Forest]], [[Feralas]], [[Duskwood]] and the [[Hinterlands]]. The branches quickly took root and became new trees, which acted like conduits, channeling the powers of the [[Emerald Dream]] into the waking world, strengthening the nearby wildlife, and scouring the saronite deposits across Ashenvale.{{Ref WoWCV1|122|124}} ===The Third War=== {{WC3-section}} [[File:Cenarius v Grommash.jpg|thumb|[[Grommash Hellscream|Grommash]] engages the demigod [[Cenarius]].]] {{Stub-section|Tyrande's missions here.}} During the [[Third War]] in 21 [[ADP]], a group of [[goblin]]s under [[Neeloc Greedyfingers]] started deforesting the area before the [[Warsong clan]] arrived, but were prevented from doing much damage by the local [[furbolg]] tribe. [[Grommash Hellscream]] and his [[orc]]s eventually acquired the goblins' aid after they repelled the furbolgs and [[Sentinels]]. At the time, the elusive [[dark troll]]s had a settlement in the region, while powerful artifacts, enclosed in circles of mushrooms, were protected by [[Forest Spirit|forest guardians]].[[The Spirits of Ashenvale (WC3 Orc)]] [[Cenarius]] restored the cut trees but was killed by [[Grommash Hellscream]] tricked by the Burning Legion masters. When the [[Burning Legion]] began its second invasion, [[Archimonde]] launched his forces into Ashenvale, with [[infernal]]s raining from the sky while thousands of [[undead]] and [[demon]]s appeared at the eastern edges of the region. The [[demon lord]] and his followers met resistance from the night elves, forest spirits, and the combined [[Horde]] and [[Alliance]] armies. Since they were fighting on separate fronts, however, the Legion easily overwhelmed them and marched steadily inland toward [[Mount Hyjal]], trampling the woodlands and all who stood in its path.{{Ref WoWCV3|75}} When [[Tyrande Whisperwind]] finally managed to wake [[Malfurion Stormrage]], the great [[archdruid]] was stunned to see what had become of Ashenvale. As [[fel]] fire consumed the forests, a toxic undead blight choked all life from the land, forcing Malfurion to quickly awake the other druids and save the wilds.{{Ref WoWCV3|76}} During their march, Archimonde commanded the corruption of Ashenvale to weaken the defenses of the kaldorei, leaving the task to the [[dreadlord]] [[Tichondrius]], who used the [[Skull of Gul'dan]] to mutate the wildlife, corrupt the ancients, and pollute the environment in the form of [[Felwood]].[[A Destiny of Flame and Sorrow (WC3 NightElf)]]{{Ref WoWCV3|77}} The [[demon hunter]] [[Illidan Stormrage]] eventually hunted down Tichondrius to consume the power of the skull, and while Felwood would remain tainted, its corruptive energies didn't spread further into the rest of Ashenvale and Hyjal.{{Ref WoWCV3|78}} At some point during the invasion of Ashenvale, an unnamed village was destroyed, along with the family of [[Vandel]], who survived as he was hunting out in the forests.''[[World of Warcraft: Illidan]]'', chapter 6 When the [[Watchers]] were fighting against [[Illidan's Naga]] on the [[Broken Isles]], [[Malfurion Stormrage]] brought [[mountain giant]]s from Ashenvale to the isles to aid [[Maiev Shadowsong]].[[Balancing the Scales (WC3 NightElf)]] ===World of Warcraft=== {{wow-section}}{{Stub/Lore-section}} In Year 25 ADP, the [[Night elf|night elves]] began a massive push to retake the forests of Ashenvale, focusing their attention on ridding their land of the [[Warsong Outriders]] once and for all. Among them, the [[Silverwing Sentinels]] answered the call and swore that they would not rest until every last [[orc]] was defeated and cast out of [[Warsong Gulch]].[[Game Guide/Battlegrounds#Warsong Gulch|Game Guide/Battlegrounds - Warsong Gulch]] Through the Silverwing [[battlemaster]]s sent across the Alliance [[capital]]s, the faction eventually recruited heroes from far and wide in order to shatter the aggressors and stop the disappearance of their precious land.[http://eu.battle.net/wow/en/game/pvp/battlegrounds/warsong-gulch Official Game Guide - Warsong Gulch] The region also faced various threats, such as the [[demon]]s of the [[Burning Legion]] lurking in [[Fire Scar Shrine]], [[Felfire Hill]], [[Demon Fall Canyon]], and [[Demon Fall Ridge]]. The vile [[satyr]] could be encountered in the ancient elven ruins of [[Xavian]], [[Night Run]], and [[Satyrnaar]]. Cursed green dragonkin soon slipped out from the [[Emerald Dream]] portal at [[Bough Shadow]], while corruption tainted the [[Ruins of Stardust]]. The Horde also seized control of several holdings in the eastern parts of the forest, and beyond their base at [[Splintertree Post]], they began to harvest trees for lumber at the [[Warsong Lumber Camp]] and the [[Warsong Labor Camp]]. During {{g|sod}}, the war between Alliance and Horde got hot as a new [[Battle for Ashenvale]] happened. Eastern Ashenvale was also home to one of the [[Nightmare Incursions]]. ===The Comic=== {{Comic-section}} In Year 26 ADP, [[Broll Bearmantle]] and [[Varian Wrynn|Lo'Gosh]] traveled to Ashenvale, where they helped [[Silverwing Sentinels]]''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic]]'', Issue 4: ''[[Balancing the Scales (comic)|Balancing the Scales]]'' and later found the corrupted [[Idol of Remulos]] in [[Thistlefur Hold]].''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic]]'', Issue 5: ''[[The Beast Within!]]'' ===Stormrage=== {{novel-section}} During the [[War Against the Nightmare]] in 27 ADP, [[Tyrande Whisperwind]] and her companions made their way into the forest of Ashenvale, where they frequently used its portal to the [[Emerald Dream]].''[[Stormrage]]'', chapter 19 ===The Shattering=== {{novel-section}} Prior to the [[Cataclysm (event)|Shattering]] in 28 ADP, two attacks happened in Ashenvale. Firstly, a horrific attack on [[Sentinel]]s by orcs of the [[Twilight's Hammer]], who skinned the elves and placed them on trees.''[[The Shattering: Prelude to Cataclysm]]'', chapter 7 Secondly, when the [[druid]]s of [[Cenarion Circle]] set up a meeting led by [[Hamuul Runetotem]] and [[Elerethe Renferal]], the cultists attacked again and slaughtered all the tauren and night elven druids.''[[The Shattering: Prelude to Cataclysm]]'', chapter 20 The only survivor of the massacre was Hamuul. As the Cataclysm was about to start, fires began to burn from lightning strikes.''[[The Shattering: Prelude to Cataclysm]]'', chapter 32 ===Wolfheart=== {{novel-section}} When [[Garrosh Hellscream]] became the new [[Warchief]] of the Horde, he sent [[orc]]ish warriors and [[goblin]] engineers into the heart of Ashenvale, where great battles were fought against [[Sentinels]] led by [[Haldrissa Woodshaper|Commander Haldrissa Woodshaper]]. Moreover, eight [[magnataur]]s and [[proto-drake]]s were brought from [[Northrend]] and released against defenseless Sentinels. The new warchief intended to build another city of the Horde in the center of Ashenvale, which would rival [[Orgrimmar]]. After many outposts fell, [[Tyrande Whisperwind]], [[Shandris Feathermoon]], the Sentinels, and the Alliance troops arrived to help relieve Haldrissa's elves, but were still unable to repel the Horde. When defeat became unavoidable, [[Varian Wrynn|King Varian Wrynn]], [[Genn Greymane|King Genn Greymane]], and the [[worgen]] of [[Gilneas (kingdom)|Gilneas]] arrived to turn the tide. The Alliance ultimately reclaimed and rebuilt [[Silverwing Outpost]], which was made the staging ground for supplying the counterattack.''[[Wolfheart]]'' ===Cataclysm=== {{cata-section}}{{Stub/Lore-section}} [[File:Astranaar Cataclysm.jpg|thumb|left|[[Astranaar]] under attack by the [[Horde]].]] In Year 28 ADP, the [[Night elf|night elves]] began to test the defenses of the [[Horde]] outposts in Ashenvale, attempting to siege both the [[Mor'shan Ramparts]] and [[Splintertree Post]].[[Mor'shan Defense]] With the arrival of reinforcements from the [[Northern Barrens]], however, the Horde forces at the ramparts were able to defeat the [[Sentinel]]s. Pushing north, the Horde took control of [[Silverwing Outpost]] while an orcish [[warlock]] poisoned the Forest Heart, allowing their troops to break the siege of [[Splintertree Post]].[[Rain of Destruction]] Meanwhile, the Horde [[adventurer]]s killed the kaldorei commanders leading the siege of [[Warsong Lumber Camp]].[[Wet Work]] After both sieges were broken, the Horde armies pressed westward, taking control of [[Silverwind Refuge]] by using a corrupted form of a [[water elemental]].[[Simmer Down Now]] They also began an attack on [[Raynewood Tower]] and [[Raynewood Retreat]], however, for each time they slayed a [[dryad]] defender, [[Keeper Ordanus]] would resurrect them as soon as they hit the ground.[[Recover the Fallen]] The Horde later started firebombing [[Astranaar]],[[Blastranaar!]] and with victory in sight, they moved in to take [[Maestra's Post]], one of the few remaining [[Alliance]] encampments. This successful campaign was short-lived, however, when the mobilized armies of [[Darnassus]] were able to break the siege of Maestra's Post,[[A Squad of Your Own]] and pushed the Horde out of Astranaar.[[Astranaar's Burning!]] The Alliance armies eventually reinforced Raynewood Retreat, killing many Horde soldiers and destroying their demolishers in the process.[[Defend the Tree!]] The Alliance heroes also rebuilt an [[Dartol's Rod|artifact]] to take control over the [[furbolgs]] near Silverwind refuge,[[True Power of the Rod]] using them to weaken the Horde army there enough for the Sentinels to retake the camp. The Alliance military then moved back eastward, cleansing the tainted Forest Heart[[The Forest Heart]] and killing the Horde overseer at the Lumber Camp. At this point, only pockets of Horde resistance remained, bringing the war full circle, in favor of the Alliance. ===Mists of Pandaria=== {{mop-section}} During the [[Alliance-Horde war]] in 30 ADP, night elves brought several caravans to [[Astranaar]] from [[Northern Barrens]] during the [[Battlefield: Barrens]]. With the dismantlement of [[Warchief]] [[Garrosh Hellscream]]'s war machine, and the conclusion of the [[Siege of Orgrimmar]], [[Tyrande Whisperwind]] allowed the Horde unimpeded access to [[Azshara]]'s lumber in return for the complete withdrawal of Horde forces from Ashenvale.[[Garrosh Hellscream (tactics)#Leader dialogue|Tyrande's dialogue after Garrosh's defeat]] ===Legion=== {{legion-section}} During the [[Burning Legion]]'s [[third invasion]] in 32 ADP, Ashenvale came under siege by [[satyr]] forces rallied under [[Rethazar the Fallen]]. Druid champions from the [[Dreamgrove]] came to deal with the satyrs.[[Powering the Portal: Ashenvale]] After they discovered that [[Archmage Vargoth]]'s [[Crystal Ball|crystal ball]] was once used by [[Grommash Hellscream]], the champions of the [[Tirisgarde]] investigated its former location in Ashenvale, where they encountered [[Maragog]] and several [[Ghostpaw Runner]]s.[[Archmage Vargoth's Travels: The Forests of Ashenvale]] ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{bfa-section|pre-expansion lore}} [[File:War of the Thorns by Sandara Tang.jpg|thumb|upright=0.85|[[Night elf|Night elven]] defenders facing [[orc]]ish invaders in the forests of Ashenvale.]] Prior to the [[War of the Thorns]] in 33 ADP, Ashenvale was considered a peaceful and boring post for a Sentinel,''[[Elegy]]'', pg. 19 until the [[Horde]] began its march to conquer [[Darnassus]]. As the [[Horde Army]] marched through Ashenvale, they faced their first resistance at [[Falfarren River]], where the kaldorei defenders led by [[Delaryn Summermoon|Captain Delaryn Summermoon]] burned down the connecting bridges of the river. When [[Varok Saurfang|High Overlord Varok Saurfang]] ordered the [[siege weapon]]s to cover the Horde soldiers trying to swim across the river, the night elf [[magi]] began to covertly destroy the siege weapons while their [[druid]]s used guerrilla warfare to reinforce hot spots. When the Horde magi froze the river, [[Malfurion Stormrage]] arrived just in time to order the Sentinels to fall back, while he and a few defenders covered their retreat from the forests.''[[Elegy]]''''[[A Good War]]'' Meanwhile, the kaldorei outposts across Ashenvale were already attacked by hundreds of rogues, while [[Lorash Sunbeam]] used poison to kill the defenders of Astranaar. After their success, Lorash lit a bonfire that burned with purple smoke and rose above the trees to signal the others to begin their assault. Many Sentinels were brought down along with their leader [[Captain Alennah Starsong]].[[Everybody Has a Price]] Despite their losses, Captain Summermoon and her forces still attempted to ambush the Horde invaders, and while they couldn't kill Saurfang in Astranaar, the attack nearly succeeded as the Horde soldiers were taken by surprise. When [[Warchief]] [[Sylvanas Windrunner]] joined the fray, however, she rallied her forces and forced the night elves to retreat once more. Unfortunately, the night elves later discovered Saurfang had survived his encounter with Malfurion. When the [[Alliance]] champions arrived, the village of Astranaar was burning with bodies littering the ground, and Captain Summermoon explained that their outposts had been taken by surprise, falling one by one. The guards were poisoned and not even the civilians were spared.[[A Disturbance in Ashenvale]] The [[Forsaken Assassin (War of the Thorns)|Forsaken Assassin]]s that still skulked within the village were dealt with as well.[[Knives of the Forsaken]] During the course of the [[Fourth War]], Alliance soldiers continued pouring into Ashenvale, reinforcing their holdings,[[Investigate Stardust Spire]] and attacking Horde outposts across the forest.[[Posting Reinforcements (Horde)]] The remaining [[Sentinels]] of Ashenvale were under the command of [[Sentinel Thenysil|Sentinel Tara Thenysil]], who the Horde attempted to eliminate, but failed to do so.[[Siege of Astranaar (Horde)]] ===Exploring Azeroth=== {{Novel-section}} Following the armistice in 34 ADP, even with its many losses, Ashenvale remained a lush wilderness filled with chittering animals, clear rivers and lakes, and towering trees.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: Kalimdor]]'', pg. 68 As the Horde continued its lumber operations at the [[Warsong Lumber Camp]], the Sentinels attacked [[Splintertree Post]]''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: Kalimdor]]'', pg. 76 and patrolled the Ashenvale border.''[[Exploring Azeroth: Kalimdor]]'', pg. 79 ==Getting there== ;{{Alliance}} Alliance: From [[Lor'danel]] in [[Darkshore]], run south along the main road into Ashenvale. Continue along the road south and then east into the main Alliance stronghold of the zone, [[Astranaar]]. ;{{Horde}} Horde: From the [[Crossroads]] in the [[Northern Barrens]], travel north to the [[Mor'shan Rampart]] and continue along the road into Ashenvale. When the road forks, head east to the Horde stronghold [[Splintertree Post]]. ==Geography== Ashenvale is a forest full of ancient trees, teeming with life. Though pockets of the forest have become tainted, overall the area is a place of deep magic and spiritual connection with nature. Several lakes are sheltered beneath the forest's boughs. A stretch of beach lines the west edge of the forest, known as the [[Zoram Strand]], where hostile [[naga]] dwell. The forest is bordered by mountains to the south, and more forest to the north. The eastern border is the [[Southfury River]]. Ashenvale contains [[Blackfathom Deeps]], an instanced dungeon located in the northwestern corner of the zone (Ashenvale, The Zoram Strand: 14.0, 15.0). In addition, the micro dungeon [[Bough Shadow]], the site of one of the [[Great Tree]]s, can be found in this zone. The Alliance entrance to the battleground [[Warsong Gulch]] is located in the southern part of the forest. Travel hubs include [[Astranaar]] and [[Forest Song]] for Alliance, and [[Splintertree Post]] and [[Zoram'gar Outpost]] for the Horde. ===Maps and subregions=== At Maestra's Post, [[Sentinel Onaeya]] fights tooth and nail against the Horde assault. In Astranaar, [[Raene Wolfrunner]] attempts to cleanse the taint that has affected the local furbolgs. At the Zoram'gar Outpost, [[Je'neu Sancrea]] sends bold adventurers into the dark Blackfathom Deeps in search of mystical items. At Forest Song, the draenei [[Vindicator Vedaar]] oversees the construction of a Draenei outpost. ==Quests== {{main|Ashenvale storyline}} Many quests in Ashenvale for both Alliance and Horde require combat with the demons and satyrs of the zone. After the Shattering, the two factions are in direct conflict, and the quests reflect this, pitching the players directly against attackers of the opposite faction. ==PvP== [[File:Silverwing Grove.jpg|thumb|[[Silverwing Grove]], base of the [[Silverwing Sentinels]].]] Alongside [[Hillsbrad Foothills]] and [[Stranglethorn Vale]], Ashenvale was one of ''the'' places for PvP combat. An Alliance attack on the Crossroads in the Barrens or a Horde attack on Astranaar would result in a back and forth match as players battled across the landscape. Ashenvale was also a prime location for high-level players to gank low-level players as for many (orcs, tauren, trolls, and night elves) this was their first contested zone. contains [[Night Elf Archaeology Fragment]]s. ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} Ashenvale Forest is also the term used for the larger forested region which includes most of western Hyjal including Azshara.''[[Shadows & Light]]'', pg. 19 ===Description=== In addition to bears and great cats prowling the dense woodlands, hulking beak-faced [[wildkin]] forage throughout Ashenvale. Vicious harpies are known to make massive nests in the tops of the tallest trees. They hunt at dawn and dusk when the light filtering through the canopy throws the forest into a confusion of shifting shadows. [[Ancient]]s - sentient trees who act as wardens of the forest - roam Ashenvale as well. Ashenvale is under the protection of ancients and the night elf sentinels. Neither had established a community as such within the forest, though, preferring to leave the vast woodlands in its natural state. Ashenvale boasted no cities; the old forest's inhabitants are primarily beasts, and there are few humanoid settlements. It is devoid of any notable ruins. Travelers through Ashenvale should treat these forces with respect, especially if they hope to reach their destination. The ancients a Cnd night elf sentinels guard Ashenvale zealously with constant patrols. Any who threaten the forest - cutting down live trees, poaching beasts of the forest, and the like - are met with the ancients' powerful attacks and the sentinels' deadly arrows. The only unified night elf presence dwelling in Ashenvale is a reclusive group of rangers, the Farstriders. They use the terrain and train other inhabitants in their specialized skills. They hold a difference of opinion amongst themselves regarding strangers in Ashenvale. Some believe that their duty is to welcome and protect travelers, as long as they show no threat to the forest. Others see any strangers as unwelcome interlopers who must be “escorted” to the southern border. Still, whatever their opinion on Ashenvale, the Farstriders bow to the wishes of the ancients and the sentinels. There is little reason to try to take the forest, since it has no cities to invade and no treasures to plunder (that anyone knows of), but the rangers and the ancients remain vigilant nonetheless.''[[Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]]'', pg. 187 After the [[Third War]], the [[Wildhammer dwarf|Wildhammer dwarves]] who traveled to Kalimdor with the Alliance founded a settlement in the [[Wildhammer peaks|southern mountains of Ashenvale]], alerting the night elves of any incursions.''[[Alliance & Horde Compendium]]'', pg. 55, 58 There's a [[demon cult]] called the [[Underblade]].
